sources.entry: Socioboard ⚠ - Social media management, analytics, and reporting platform supporting nine social media networks out-of-the-box. GPL-3.0 Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Socioboard 5.0 is a self-hostable social media management, scheduling, analytics and reporting platform built on Node.js with a PHP frontend, listed in awesome-selfhosted under Analytics.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Socioboard as a social media management and content marketing platform for managing multiple social accounts from one place. It mentions creating, planning and scheduling posts, automating post timing, and assigning tasks and managing permissions for team members. Analytics features include pre-built reports and custom reports, plus automatic email reports of dashboard statistics, team reports and account data. It also has an RSS feed section with search, sorting and filtering, and it states support for nine social networks. The README says the Socioboard 5.0 backend is a centralized API in Node.js, Express, Mongoose and Sequelize ORM, with a PHP frontend. Configuration links for 5.0 are marked as "to be added soon," and the README points to a separate INSTALLATION.md file for setup. The README also says a commercial SaaS version exists alongside the open source Socioboard Core.
use_cases: schedule social media posts across multiple accounts
manage team social media tasks and permissions
generate social media analytics and reports
receive automatic email reports of social statistics
curate content from RSS feeds for social sharing
self-host a social media management tool
how_to_run: Follow the steps in the INSTALLATION.md file in the repository (the README links to it for SocioBoard 5.0)
notable: Supports nine social media networks out of the box, according to the README
Auto email reports of dashboard, team and account statistics
RSS feed aggregation with search, sort and category filtering
Extensible through plugins, per the README's description of Socioboard Core
Commercial SaaS version offered alongside the open source edition
caveats: The README says the Socioboard 5.0 configuration links 'will be added soon,' so setup documentation is incomplete in the README itself
Developer documentation in the README refers to Socioboard 4.0 docs, and the 5.0 install guide is only referenced via INSTALLATION.md
The awesome-selfhosted listing marks the project with a warning symbol, which the listing does not explain
